openItems.why: Ends pen-register suits over trackers from Jan 1, 2027; wiretap claims survive either way, so the plan doesn't change.
Filed March 2025 with a $25M revenue floor; no sign it passed.
Would tax digital products from Jan 1, 2027; final status unknown.

openItems.item: NC sales tax on custom printing and delivery
openItems.why: No primary source; two NCDOR matrices conflict.

openItems.item: Budgeting app under the FTC Safeguards Rule
openItems.why: Unresolved for apps that pull bank data through an aggregator.
NC G.S. 66-57.1 doesn't protect inventions related to the employer's business; the employment agreement controls.
Built around a prior employer's work, per your notes.

openItems.item: Chrome Web Store, Copilot Studio and startup-program terms

items.title: MFA on every account
items.claim: Passkeys or TOTP on GitHub, npm, hosting, DNS/registrar, Cloudflare, payment, email and admin accounts; registrar lock and auto-renew.

items.title: Spend caps on cloud and AI providers
items.claim: Each app has its own provider project or workspace with a hard cap, plus alerts.

items.title: Credential rotation list
items.claim: Every token, where it lives and how to revoke it — the first thing needed after a poisoned install or a leak.

items.title: Employment agreement reviewed
items.claim: An employment lawyer has read the assignment, outside-activity and choice-of-law clauses before an AI-tooling venture launches. NC G.S. 66-57.1's exception for work related to the employer's business is the one that bites.

items.title: Data class and data map written
items.claim: Exactly what data the product can read or collect, where it is stored and for how long. It drives the privacy policy and every security answer.

items.title: IP ownership of the origin confirmed in writing
items.claim: Ownership of the code's origin (built around prior-employer work, per your notes) is confirmed in writing, ideally lawyer-reviewed, before distributing to anyone.

items.title: Name and trademark cleared
items.claim: A USPTO search for the product name; the owning LLC is decided.

items.title: Authorization in every route handler
items.claim: Every API route handler checks who is calling, inside the handler. Middleware does not cover /api, and CVE-2025-29927 showed middleware can be skipped entirely. This class hit four of your codebases.

items.title: Auth fails closed
items.claim: No auth or secret check sits in a try/catch that lets the request through on error.

items.title: No secrets in the repo
items.claim: No keys or tokens in source files, and env files are ignored by git. (A history scan, e.g. gitleaks, is attached as evidence separately.)

items.title: No unescaped JSON inside <script>
items.claim: JSON.stringify does not escape < > /, so author data inlined into a script tag can break out (the StackDive XSS, copied into five locations).

items.title: Rate limits and quotas on costly endpoints
items.claim: AI, email and anonymous endpoints are rate-limited per user or key; provider caps alone stop every user at once.

items.title: Errors don't leak internals
items.claim: Responses carry a generic error; detail goes to server logs (StackDive's /api/health leaked Neon host and role).

items.title: Security headers baseline
items.claim: nosniff, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, a restrictive Permissions-Policy, HSTS (no preload yet) and a CSP with frame-ancestors; no 'unsafe-eval'.

items.title: Server-side URL fetches are guarded
items.claim: Any fetch of a caller-supplied URL blocks private and link-local ranges and validates redirects.

items.title: Row-level security applied, not just written
items.claim: RLS is enabled with policies on exposed tables, service-role keys stay server-side, and views use security_invoker.

items.title: Dependency install policy
items.claim: A committed lockfile, plus a release-age delay and an install-script allowlist (pnpm 11 defaults or npm 12) — the defence against poisoned packages.

items.title: Next.js and React patched
items.claim: Not on a version affected by CVE-2025-29927 or React2Shell. Confirm the latest patched versions at launch — the research found no 2026 advisories.

items.title: Bot challenge on sign-up, login and anonymous AI
items.claim: Turnstile (free, unlimited) or similar on the endpoints bots abuse.

items.title: MCP server follows the security best practices
items.claim: No token passthrough, per-client consent, exact redirect matching, minimal scopes, SSRF defences.

items.title: Page and document content is treated as hostile
items.claim: Anything the product reads can carry prompt injection: agents get the least tool access that works, and content never triggers a privileged action without a check.

items.title: Extension permissions are minimal and disclosed
items.claim: Every permission in the manifest is named in the privacy policy, and none is requested without a use (your Farxplor policy↔manifest contract, generalised).

items.title: Privacy policy published
items.claim: A privacy policy page exists and is linked.

items.title: Terms of service published
items.claim: A terms page exists for public products.

items.title: The policy matches what the product does
items.claim: The FTC holds you to every privacy promise, express or implied. Every processor the code sends data to is named; nothing is promised that isn't built.

items.title: No unqualified security or sharing claims
items.claim: No "bank-level security", "military-grade" or "we never share data" — the classic FTC deception pattern (the report's inference).

items.title: Age statement, and no knowing collection from under-13s
items.claim: The terms or policy state an age floor (13+ or 18+). Gemini-backed apps must be 18+. COPPA applies with actual knowledge of under-13 users.

items.title: AI is disclosed to users
items.claim: A persistent "AI assistant" label; Anthropic's usage policy requires consumer-facing chatbots to disclose AI at the start of each session.

items.title: Users told to verify AI output
items.claim: Anthropic's commercial terms require telling users to verify factual outputs.

items.title: No ad pixels or session replay
items.claim: Third-party ad pixels, chat widgets and session replay are where small sites get sued (California wiretap claims survive SB 690). First-party analytics only, or load after consent and disclose.

items.title: Global Privacy Control honoured
items.claim: Cheap to honour, and California treats it as a valid opt-out for covered businesses.

items.title: Account deletion exists if it is promised
items.claim: If the policy promises deletion (StackDive's does), a deletion route exists — even an email address. An unkept promise is deception.

items.title: Marketing email: postal address and one-click unsubscribe
items.claim: CAN-SPAM covers all commercial email, B2B included; opt-outs honoured within 10 business days.

items.title: Breach plan with a 30-day clock
items.claim: Obligations follow residents, not you: California's 30 calendar days is the working clock; NC also requires notice to the AG.

items.title: Chrome Web Store policies read and met
items.claim: Store developer policies were not covered by the research — read them before submitting.

items.title: SPF, DKIM and DMARC
items.claim: Required by Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft for bulk senders; start DMARC at p=none with reports.

items.title: Offsite backup and one restore test
items.claim: Database backups don't include stored files; a nightly dump plus files copied separately, and one timed restore.

items.title: Error tracking and uptime checks
items.claim: Free tiers cover a solo operator (Sentry, UptimeRobot, Better Stack).

items.title: One-page incident runbook
items.claim: Kill switch, credential rotation list, restore steps, who decides on notification.

items.title: security.txt with Contact and an unexpired Expires
items.claim: RFC 9116 needs only Contact and Expires — and an expired file is worse than none.

items.title: WCAG 2.2 AA on key flows
items.claim: Including focus-not-obscured and 24×24 px targets; overlays are no shield. Automated hints are attached; a real audit is the evidence.

items.title: ZAP baseline and Observatory header check
items.claim: Both are passive and safe against production.

items.title: Hosted checkout (PCI SAQ A)
items.claim: Stripe Checkout or Elements, webhook signatures verified, no analytics or tag scripts on payment pages.

items.title: Soft launch with a rollback plan
items.claim: A small cohort first; errors and spend within limits before access widens.

items.title: Gated release: own accounts → named pilot → wider
items.claim: Each step has a rollback path.

items.title: Recurring routines scheduled
items.claim: Weekly advisories and spend; monthly backups and DMARC reports; quarterly restore, access review, ZAP and WCAG retest.

items.title: Enterprise security packet
items.claim: Current architecture diagram, data flow, subprocessors and incident process, ready for security reviewers.

items.title: HSTS preload, last
items.claim: Removal takes months, so preload comes after everything else is stable.

items.title: CSRF defence on state-changing requests
items.claim: SameSite cookies layered with an Origin or Fetch-Metadata check on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. XSS defeats every CSRF defence, so this sits on top of output escaping, not instead of it.

items.title: File uploads are constrained
items.claim: Extension allowlist, server-generated filenames, private storage, size limits, and authentication before upload.

items.title: CSP chosen deliberately
items.claim: Nonce-based CSP forces dynamic rendering and loses CDN caching; authenticated apps and stores choose nonce or SRI on purpose, static marketing sites can take a simpler policy.

items.title: VPS: Docker ports, sockets and users
items.claim: Published Docker ports bypass UFW — bind internal services to 127.0.0.1 or a private network, never mount the Docker socket, run as non-root with no-new-privileges, and turn on unattended security upgrades.

items.title: Staging exists, with separate keys, and is noindexed
items.claim: A staging environment with its own secrets and data, marked noindex, so tests never touch production.

items.title: Object-level access tested as a second user
items.claim: Sign in as a second user and try to read or change the first user's records by ID. Broken Access Control is OWASP's #1.

items.title: Per-user AI quotas in the app
items.claim: Provider caps stop every user at once; each user also gets a daily allowance in the app.

items.title: CAA records, DNSSEC and no dangling records
items.claim: CAA limits who can issue certificates; remove DNS records before deleting the hosting they point at (subdomain takeover); keep a domain and subdomain inventory.

items.title: CalOPPA privacy-policy contents
items.claim: California requires a conspicuously posted policy that lists the categories collected, third parties shared with, how users review or change data, how Do Not Track is handled, and an effective date.

items.title: Subscriptions: California auto-renewal disclosures and online cancel
items.claim: Clear renewal terms before purchase, affirmative consent, an acknowledgement, and online cancellation (California ARL); Virginia's law also requires cancelling to be as easy as signing up.

sources.title: California Automatic Renewal Law, Bus. & Prof. Code §17600 et seq.

items.title: No dark patterns
items.claim: No fake scarcity, drip pricing, buried privacy toggles or hard cancellation — a live FTC enforcement theme.

items.title: No companion personas; human review on consequential decisions
items.claim: California SB 243 regulates companion chatbots with a private right of action; OpenAI and Anthropic policies bar automated consequential decisions without human oversight.

items.title: No warranty of exclusive ownership of AI-generated work
items.claim: The human-authorship requirement stands (Thaler cert denied, March 2026); terms and contracts must not promise exclusive ownership of mostly AI-generated output.

sources.title: Thaler cert denied — human authorship (Mayer Brown)

items.title: EU scope avoided by policy (or handled)
items.claim: GDPR reaches services offered to people in the EU. If the EU isn't a market: USD pricing, English only, no EU marketing — and say so.

items.title: SMS out of scope until counsel or a compliant vendor
items.claim: Texting needs prior express written consent, with $500–$1,500 statutory damages per message.

items.title: Dated accessibility statement with a feedback contact
items.claim: Pair the WCAG 2.2 AA work with a public, dated statement; overlays are no shield (FTC accessiBe order).

items.title: Core Web Vitals in the good range
items.claim: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1 at the 75th percentile.

items.title: Data minimisation: no SSNs, no bank credentials
items.claim: Never store Social Security numbers or bank credentials; link accounts only through a compliant aggregator.

items.title: Personal data encrypted at rest
items.claim: Virginia's and North Carolina's breach triggers involve unencrypted data — encryption shrinks exposure sharply.

items.title: Children: parental consent, or no personal information from under-13s
items.claim: COPPA's amended rule has been mandatory since April 22, 2026, with written retention and security-program requirements; no household exemption was found.

sources.title: Amended COPPA rule in effect (Bass Berry)

items.title: Counsel on the Safeguards Rule before adding financial features
items.claim: Whether a budgeting app that pulls bank data through an aggregator is a 'financial institution' is unresolved — ask before opening it to others.

items.title: Short plain-language privacy note
items.claim: What is stored, who sees it, how to delete — and keep every promise.

items.title: Signed MSA and SOW (lawyer-reviewed once)
items.claim: IP transfers on payment, pre-existing components (the reference architecture) licensed not assigned, liability cap, client indemnity for supplied content, scope and revision limits, maintenance terms.

items.title: DPA and ownership of domain, hosting and credentials decided
items.claim: Data-processing terms when the site collects user data; the contract says who owns the domain, registrar, hosting and credentials.

items.title: License inventory: no AGPL/GPL in handed-over code
items.claim: Handing over a built theme or app is distribution; list dependency, theme, font and image licenses.

items.title: Handover: credentials, registrar lock, restore test, written acceptance
items.claim: Transfer credentials and code, lock the registrar, prove a restore works, get acceptance in writing.

items.title: Public-entity clients: DOJ Title II web rule
items.claim: Government clients must meet WCAG under the Title II rule from 2027 or 2028 depending on size.

sources.title: DOJ Title II web rule deadlines (Plante Moran)

items.title: E&O / cyber insurance quoted
items.claim: Live quotes for general liability and tech E&O (cyber overlaps E&O — don't add them).

items.title: DMCA agent designated (sites hosting user content)
items.claim: Register the agent and renew every three years.

items.title: CPA answer on NC sales tax for custom printing and shipping
items.claim: No primary source covered NC taxability of custom printing or embroidery, and two NCDOR matrices disagree on delivery charges.

items.title: Registered for NC sales tax before the first sale
items.claim: 4.75% state plus county, destination-based; VA and NC economic nexus at $100,000 for out-of-state buyers.

items.title: Original art or written licenses only
items.claim: Stripe prohibits unlicensed branded goods — one bad design can cost the whole account.

items.title: Textile Act labels kept or replaced
items.claim: Keep supplier neck labels intact, or replace them with your name/RN and required content and keep records of removed labels for three years.

sources.title: FTC textile and wool labeling guide

items.title: Accurate origin claims
items.claim: No unqualified "Made in USA" on imported blanks — "Printed in USA on imported blank".

items.title: Shipping, lead times, delays, refunds published
items.claim: With no stated time the Mail Order Rule default is 30 days; delays need a notice with a free cancel-and-refund option; refunds due within 7 working days.

sources.title: FTC Mail, Internet or Telephone Order Rule

items.title: No seeded or incentivised reviews
items.claim: The FTC's fake-review rule has applied since October 21, 2024.

items.title: Stripe webhooks verified, TLS 1.2+
items.claim: Verify every webhook signature; no third-party scripts on payment pages.

items.title: One real low-value order end to end
items.claim: Payment, tax charged, confirmation email, label check on the finished garment, refund.

items.title: US-only shipping stated
items.claim: Keeps EU consumer law and the European Accessibility Act out of scope.

items.title: LLC owns the product and its code; EIN; annual report calendar
items.claim: Decide which LLC owns each product. Domestic LLCs no longer file BOI reports (FinCEN, final rule Aug 2026). VA $50/yr; NC $200/yr (secondary source).

items.title: Targeted professional reviews booked where they pay
items.claim: Lawyer once on the client contract set; employment lawyer on the job agreement and the Xplor origin; CPA on NC sales tax; counsel before financial data, children's data or SMS.

items.title: Weekly: security advisories and dependency updates
items.claim: Exploitation is the top breach entry point (31% per DBIR 2026); patch framework CVEs fast.

items.title: Weekly: errors, uptime, AI and cloud spend against caps
items.claim: Check the error tracker, uptime monitor and spend.

items.title: Monthly: read DMARC reports; tighten none → quarantine → reject
items.claim: Move the policy up only when reports are clean.

items.title: Monthly: backups ran, files backed up separately
items.claim: Database backups don't include stored files.

items.title: Monthly: sales-tax filing and payout reconciliation; 1099-K tracking
items.claim: Reconcile against payouts; the 1099-K threshold is $20,000 and 200 transactions, and income is taxable either way.

items.title: Answer chargebacks inside the 7–21 day window
items.claim: Disputes cost a non-refundable fee and have short deadlines.

items.title: Quarterly: restore a backup into scratch and time it
items.claim: A backup you haven't restored is a hope.

items.title: Quarterly: access review and secret rotation
items.claim: Remove people who left; rotate shared secrets and tokens from the rotation list.

items.title: Quarterly: ZAP baseline, header check, WCAG retest
items.claim: Passive scans are safe against production.

items.title: Annual: LLC reports, insurance renewal, policies vs reality, security.txt Expires
items.claim: Refresh the security.txt Expires date before it lapses — an expired file is worse than none.
